metadata.notes: Historical, international, atmospheric transport and uncommon hazards. No original alternate IDs modified; deferred strong but repetitive tornado and blizzard choices.

reviews.title_after: The Hunga Tonga eruption sends a pressure wave around Earth
reviews.location_after: Hunga Tonga–Hunga Haʻapai, Tonga; global atmosphere
reviews.core_fact: A climactic underwater volcanic eruption at Hunga Tonga on January 15, 2022 launched atmospheric pressure waves detected worldwide.
reviews.source_dependence: NOAA event observations and USGS-reviewed seismoacoustic observations corroborate the dated eruption and wave; instrument methods and datasets differ.
reviews.unverified_cautions: A volcanic eruption caused the wave; it was not a tropical cyclone or a conventional atmospheric storm. Distinguish eruption local time, UTC, Lamb-wave arrival times and later tsunami arrivals.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original global Lamb-wave arrival map and barometer pressure traces

reviews.title_before: Winter Weather — POTOMAC / SEELEY LAKE REGION, Montana
reviews.title_after: Record heat and violent winds fuel Australia's Black Saturday bushfires
reviews.core_fact: Extreme temperatures, prolonged drought and powerful winds coincided with catastrophic bushfires in Victoria on February 7, 2009.
reviews.source_dependence: Bureau of Meteorology station/climate summaries and Victoria's Country Fire Authority incident archives are separate agency source types, though subsequent retrospectives overlap.
reviews.unverified_cautions: CFA's total losses cover multiple fires, not a single ignition or weather station. A wind shift, prior drought, human ignitions and pyroconvection are distinct explanatory components; do not imply heat alone ignited fires.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Feb7 dry-heat and wind-change schematic over Victorian fire regions

reviews.title_before: Winter Weather — SOUTH CENTRAL UTAH, Utah
reviews.title_after: A deadly tornado outbreak tears across Alabama during the Great Depression
reviews.location_after: Alabama and the Deep South, United States
reviews.core_fact: Multiple devastating tornadoes crossed Alabama and surrounding Deep South states on March 21, 1932.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS Birmingham historical reconstruction and the independently edited Encyclopedia of Alabama corroborate the date and multi-tornado scope, but both depend partly on incomplete historical reports.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Exact outbreak tornado count, fatalities, individual track continuity and F ratings are uncertain in 1932-era records. Do not treat county reports as separately surveyed modern tornadoes or claim an exact universal death toll.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original 1932 historical path/impacted-county schematic, uncertainty dashed

reviews.title_after: Winds begin spreading the Chernobyl plume after the reactor disaster
reviews.location_after: Chernobyl, northern Ukraine (then Soviet Union); northern Europe
reviews.core_fact: The Chernobyl reactor accident began on April 26, 1986, releasing material to the atmosphere; wind later carried airborne radionuclides over northern Europe.
reviews.source_dependence: OECD/NEA's accident and dispersion assessment plus a separately documented Swedish meteorological deposition analysis confirm the release date and weather-controlled transport; both draw on historical radiological measurements.
reviews.unverified_cautions: This is weather's role in a technological disaster, not a weather-caused reactor accident. The first Swedish measurements followed after April 26; varying winds and rainfall/deposition covered several days. Distinguish atmospheric release from measured fallout date.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original 26 April start and subsequent transport schematic with changing flow and wet deposition

reviews.title_after: A violent hailstorm strikes Moradabad, India's historic weather disaster
reviews.core_fact: A destructive hailstorm struck the Moradabad region of northern India on April 30, 1888; WMO recognizes it for the highest reported historical hailstorm death toll.
reviews.source_dependence: WMO extremes-panel review and Royal Meteorological Society's separate explainer report the same dated historical event; not independent 1888 observations, relying on historical books and correspondence.
reviews.unverified_cautions: WMO's historical estimate of 246 deaths combines Moradabad and Bareilly; it is not a contemporary instrument measurement, nor a current modern-observing-network comparison. Hail size and casualties must be presented as historical reports with uncertainty.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original old-era northern India location and documented hailstorm casualty-scope schematic

reviews.title_after: Giant hail slams Fort Worth's Mayfest outdoor festival
reviews.core_fact: A destructive high-precipitation supercell brought very large hail and flash flooding to the Dallas–Fort Worth area on May 5, 1995, striking the Mayfest event.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS retrospective and AMS case-study abstract independently present the storm narrative but authors use overlapping NOAA Storm Data and radar evidence.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Storm-scale hail swath, Mayfest injuries, flash-flood deaths and metropolitan economic losses refer to different exposure areas and time periods; avoid one combined single-hazard count. Avoid copying historic news photographs.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Mayfest HP supercell path, hail swath and urban-flash-flood process timeline

reviews.title_after: A flash flood surges through Shadyside, Ohio, after intense storms
reviews.location_after: Shadyside, Pipe and Wegee Creeks, Belmont County, Ohio
reviews.core_fact: Intense thunderstorms triggered catastrophic flash flooding in the Pipe and Wegee Creek basins near Shadyside on June 14, 1990.
reviews.source_dependence: USGS field hydrology and runoff reconstruction and NOAA/NWS disaster-weather studies independently document the occurrence; some flood-impact statistics ultimately trace common damage surveys.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The flood began June 14 while USGS hydrologic study covers June 14–15; separate gauge peak, rainfall rate and final fatality counts. The event includes two creek basins rather than a citywide uniform crest.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Pipe/Wegee watershed, small-basin runoff concentration and flood-wave schematic

reviews.title_after: A violent tornado cuts through Regina, Saskatchewan
reviews.core_fact: A destructive tornado struck Regina, Saskatchewan, on June 30, 1912, with severe impacts in the city's built-up neighborhoods.
reviews.source_dependence: Provincial Archives holds dated records and the City of Regina separately confirms the anniversary; historical ratings, fatalities and path depictions originate from overlapping early archival accounts.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Historic 'cyclone' is a tornado, not tropical cyclone. Later assigned F4 is retrospective, not a 1912 EF rating; reconcile 'two funnels' language with one or multiple true tracks before drawing.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original downtown Regina surveyed historic path and annotated archival reference map

reviews.title_after: The Fourth of July of 1911 brings extraordinary New England heat
reviews.core_fact: New England experienced exceptional, often record-setting heat on July 4, 1911, including a 104°F observation historically attributed to Boston.
reviews.source_dependence: Two distinct NWS historical compilations corroborate July 4 heat, while contemporaneous climate-station metadata and exposure corrections remain to be checked; same institutional family.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The multiday 1911 heat wave was not confined to July 4; station siting/observation practices and historical state-record revisions must be reconciled. Avoid asserting exact multistate mortality for July4 only.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original dated July 4 station highs across New England with record-period caveats

reviews.title_before: Excessive Heat — TUCSON METRO AREA, Arizona
reviews.title_after: Hurricane Beryl makes landfall near Matagorda, Texas
reviews.location_after: Matagorda area, upper Texas Gulf Coast
reviews.core_fact: Hurricane Beryl made landfall near Matagorda, Texas, on the morning of July 8, 2024 as a Category 1 hurricane.
reviews.source_dependence: Contemporaneous NHC advisory, NWS Houston event summary and NASA satellite interpretation establish the local event/date; NHC and NWS share NOAA cyclone intensity analysis.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Operational 80 mph landfall statement and finalized 80-knot assessment are different intensity estimates; do not conflate knots and mph or dated warnings with post-analysis. Separate landfall winds from inland rainfall and tornadoes.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Texas landfall center track, wind field and contemporaneous observation time windows

reviews.title_before: Strong Wind — COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE, California
reviews.title_after: Lightning ignites a deadly oil-depot fire amid flooding in Dronka, Egypt
reviews.core_fact: Severe thunderstorms on November 2, 1994 were associated with lightning striking an oil depot near Dronka, Egypt; flooding carried burning fuel into surrounding areas.
reviews.source_dependence: WMO's retrospective extremes committee and UPI contemporaneous coverage separately document the date, weather and fire; UPI's early death estimates are provisional, not WMO's later finalized 469.
reviews.unverified_cautions: WMO classifies this as indirect lightning mortality in a fuel-fire/flood disaster, not hundreds directly struck by lightning. Contemporaneous counts differ from final adopted figures; confirm reservoir/flash-flood mechanism before mapping.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original schematic of storm lightning, ignited fuel and flood-driven downstream spread
